query.description: Pipeline outcomes, daily reliability, signal outcomes, and failure classes.
query.sql: SELECT status, signal, trade_date, error_message FROM public.pipeline_runs;
metric_definitions: Completion rate = completed pipeline runs divided by all pipeline runs.
HOLD share = completed runs whose final signal is HOLD divided by all completed runs.

query.description: Strategy inventory, lifecycle state, thesis coverage, backtest configuration, and persisted evidence.
query.sql: SELECT s.id, s.ticker, s.name, s.status, s.is_active, s.active_thesis, bc.id AS backtest_config_id, br.id AS backtest_run_id, br.metrics, br.trade_log, br.simulation_version, br.input_hash FROM public.strategies s LEFT JOIN public.backtest_configs bc ON bc.strategy_id = s.id LEFT JOIN public.backtest_runs br ON br.backtest_config_id = bc.id;
metric_definitions: Backtest coverage = persisted backtest runs divided by configured backtests.

query.description: Agent-decision volume, token usage, and recorded cost.
query.sql: SELECT count(*) AS decisions, sum(coalesce(prompt_tokens,0)) AS prompt_tokens, sum(coalesce(completion_tokens,0)) AS completion_tokens, sum(coalesce(cost_usd,0)) AS recorded_cost_usd FROM public.agent_decisions;
metric_definitions: Total tokens = prompt tokens plus completion tokens.
Recorded model cost excludes any cost not written to cost_usd.

query.description: Closed stock cash P&L, closed Kalshi position P&L, and open-position marking coverage.
query.sql: WITH stock AS (SELECT sum(CASE WHEN side='sell' THEN quantity*price ELSE -quantity*price END)-sum(coalesce(fee,0)) AS realized_pnl FROM public.trades WHERE ticker NOT LIKE 'KX%'), kalshi AS (SELECT sum(coalesce(realized_pnl,0)) AS realized_pnl FROM public.positions WHERE closed_at IS NOT NULL), open_kalshi AS (SELECT count(*) AS open_positions, count(*) FILTER (WHERE current_price IS NULL) AS unmarked_positions FROM public.positions WHERE closed_at IS NULL) SELECT stock.realized_pnl AS stock_realized_pnl, kalshi.realized_pnl AS kalshi_realized_pnl, stock.realized_pnl+kalshi.realized_pnl AS known_realized_net, open_kalshi.open_positions, open_kalshi.unmarked_positions FROM stock, kalshi, open_kalshi;
metric_definitions: Known realized net is a narrow arithmetic reconciliation, not a consolidated portfolio return.

blocks.body:
# Augr Profitability Audit: Why It Has Not Produced a Defensible Edge

**Audit date:** August 14, 2026  
**Scope:** live paper database, code, prior audits, the complete `docs/Augr Trading Research` synthesis, current exchange mechanics, and empirical strategy research.  
**Decision:** do not add capital or enable live autonomous execution yet.

## Executive Summary

**Augr still has no defensible after-cost edge.** The system generated 171 nominally active strategies and 40,650 agent decisions, consumed 184.9 million tracked tokens, and persisted 7,442 pipeline runs. Yet only one backtest run exists, only three stock campaigns and two Kalshi lots are closed, and 99.35% of completed runs ended in HOLD.

**The visible ledger is barely positive before missing costs.** Known closed results are approximately +$17.86: +$135.50 in SNAL, CCL, and TSCO, offset by −$117.65 on closed Kalshi lots. Ten Kalshi positions lack current marks, every recorded trade fee is zero, and model cost is recorded as zero.

**The new 13F replication MVP is promising infrastructure, not new profitability evidence.** It correctly uses deterministic, paper-only targets and preserves disclosure timing, mapping, and intent provenance. It has no deployed observations or historical performance, and its current price, spread, turnover, execution-cost, and attribution gaps would overstate results.

**Recommendation:** freeze legacy discovery, fix the common ledger and simulator, harden copy trading, and evaluate a small deterministic portfolio: benchmark core, quality-filtered wheel, momentum/trend, selected 13F replication, and tiny prediction-market experiments. LLMs should remain outside every order hot path.

## What ‘Not Profitable’ Actually Means

There are three questions. **Closed trades:** barely positive before missing costs. **Benchmark outperformance:** unknown because Augr lacks a consolidated time-weighted equity curve, external-flow ledger, current marking, and strategy attribution. **Economic value after all costs:** almost certainly negative because $17.86 cannot cover operating and opportunity costs.

The correct conclusion is **no defensible profitability**, not proven negative alpha. The sample is too small to estimate an edge, while missing costs and marks bias the visible result upward.

## The Trading Factory Usually Does Not Reach a Tradable Decision

The pipeline failed on 4,997 of 7,442 runs (67.1%). An unavailable Ollama host caused 4,287 failures; a Kalshi snapshot constraint caused 397; position limits rejected at least 156 after ten stale or unmarked Kalshi positions accumulated. Recent completion recovered to 73%–78%, still below a reasonable 95% production target.

## The Decision Funnel Collapses Into HOLD

Of 2,445 completed runs, 2,429 ended in HOLD, 12 in BUY, and 4 in SELL. The stock side emitted no BUY final signals in the reviewed set. Separately, 71 portfolio opportunities were recorded: 51 rejected, 20 expired, none selected or ordered. This is not proven discipline; it is consistent with disconnected portfolio context, late risk rejection, and no calibrated mapping from confidence to expected return.

## Strategy Breadth Is Masquerading as Evidence

All 171 strategies have `is_active = true`, even though 42 also have `status = paused`. None has a populated active thesis. Nine WDC variants and other duplicate families create multiple-testing and scheduling ambiguity.

One hundred ten backtest configs exist, but only one run was persisted. That ORCL test made one round trip: +1.01% over five years while buy-and-hold returned +149.10%. Stored 80% win rate and 401.8 profit factor are bar-return statistics, not closed-trade statistics. One zero-fee trade in a legacy-unversioned simulation is not evidence.

## Root-Cause Audit

The primary failure is a **research-to-execution governance gap**. Augr’s own synthesis recommends fair value, net edge after costs, sizing, execution, journaling, calibration, and regime control. The running implementation skipped from generated narratives or arbitrary threshold rules to unrealistic paper fills.

Verified findings include pipeline failures, HOLD concentration, sparse backtesting, duplicated lifecycle state, zero thesis coverage, unmarked positions, zero-cost paper defaults, and misleading backtest metrics. Likely—but not directly measurable—is negative economic P&L after operating cost. True consolidated return, exact operating cost, option assignment exposure, and live fill quality remain unresolved because the required data is absent.

## Copy Trading Improves the Architecture, but It Does Not Yet Add an Edge

The stock copy-trading MVP on `main` is a meaningful improvement over Augr’s legacy strategy factory. It ingests SEC 13F holdings, creates immutable observations, requires reviewed CUSIP mappings, preserves unmapped and excluded weight as cash, calculates targets deterministically, isolates positions by subscription-backed strategy, routes orders through global risk, and prohibits live trading. The full Go test suite passes.

The strategy itself remains unvalidated. A 13F is a delayed quarter-end holdings snapshot, not a trade feed. The SEC permits filing up to 45 days after quarter end, and confidential-treatment requests can omit positions for longer; see the [SEC Form 13F FAQ](https://www.sec.gov/rules-regulations/staff-guidance/division-investment-management-frequently-asked-questions/frequently-asked-questions-about-form-13f). Academic copycat research shows disclosed-portfolio replication can sometimes approach the target fund’s return after costs, but that does not establish benchmark alpha for Augr’s selected managers or implementation; see [NBER’s Copycat Funds](https://www.nber.org/papers/w8653).

Four code gaps are profitability-critical. First, the price provider uses the latest daily close and never rejects a stale `ObservedAt`; it supplies no bid/ask spread, so `MaxSpreadBPS` effectively compares against zero. Second, the 25% turnover cap scales only the rebalance triggered by a new filing; automatic sync does not work down residual drift on later sessions. Third, execution reuses the immediate-fill paper broker whose fee and slippage defaults are zero. Fourth, the implementation creates a backing strategy per subscription instead of the generic `copy_subscription` origin envisioned by the design.

**Decision:** retain the feature in paper mode and promote it into the edge lab only after point-in-time multi-filing replay, quote-based execution, multi-session reconciliation, and exact cost/attribution are implemented. Production is still at schema 62, so migration 63 has produced no live paper evidence in the audited database.

## Prediction-Market Failure: Fabricated Edge and Non-Executable Size

Legacy Kalshi decisions reused fair probability 0.88 across unrelated contracts priced $0.003–$0.034, creating apparent 84.5%–87.7% edges. Probability was uncalibrated; volume or open interest stood in for executable depth; the paper broker bought hundreds of thousands of contracts with zero fees and immediate fills.

Current [Kalshi fees](https://kalshi.com/docs/kalshi-fee-schedule.pdf) and [Polymarket CLOB V2](https://docs.polymarket.com/v2-migration) mechanics make exact fee lookup, book size, latency, partial fills, capital lockup, and resolution rules mandatory. A recent [executable arbitrage reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00666) also shows why headline theoretical arbitrage can shrink dramatically when fills are modeled.

## Strategy Recommendations

The replacement portfolio should be boring at the core and experimental at the edge. Strong candidates are a quality-filtered wheel, cross-sectional momentum plus quality/low volatility, time-series trend, selected 13F replication, defined-risk volatility premium, complete-set prediction arbitrage, maker-first event-market quoting, and calibrated weather/macro models. Momentum persistence is documented by [Jegadeesh and Titman](https://www.nber.org/papers/w7159), and value/momentum evidence spans markets in [Asness, Moskowitz, and Pedersen](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/jofi.12021).

A research-capital template—not personal investment advice—is 60%–80% passive benchmark core, 10%–20% wheel, 10%–20% momentum/trend, 0%–10% selected 13F replication after validation, and 0%–5% prediction-market experiments. Experimental sleeves must fit inside the total risk budget rather than summing mechanically to more than 100%.

## The Wheel: Use It, but Benchmark It Honestly

The wheel is repeated short-put exposure followed by covered calls after assignment. Premium is not alpha. Cboe’s long-run [PUT, BXM, and BXMD benchmarks](https://www.cboe.com/us/indices/benchmark_indices/) and [options benchmark study](https://cdn.cboe.com/resources/spx/wilshire-options-based-benchmark-indexes-2019.pdf) show lower volatility and drawdown can come with capped upside and bull-market underperformance.

### Deterministic rules

- Use liquid broad ETFs or a tiny approved list of profitable, liquid companies the portfolio will own.
- Sell 20–30 delta cash-secured puts, usually 30–45 DTE, only when implied volatility clears a conservative realized-volatility forecast.
- Avoid single-stock earnings; use defined-risk put spreads when gap or capital risk is high.
- After assignment, sell 15–25 delta calls above the desired exit; never roll indefinitely to hide a loss.
- Cap each underlying at 5%–10% of capital and total short-volatility exposure at 20%–30%; prohibit naked options and margin-dependent rescues.
- Model early assignment, dividends, pin risk, taxes, spread, and buying power. Short equity options can be assigned before expiry; see [FINRA](https://www.finra.org/investors/insights/trading-options-understanding-assignment).

Reject the sleeve unless after-cost out-of-sample total return, Sortino, expected shortfall, and recovery time are competitive with PUT/BXM/BXMD.

## Prediction-Market Playbook

1. **Complete-set/combinatorial arbitrage:** reserve every leg; include orphan-leg loss in worst-case P&L.
2. **Exact cross-venue arbitrage:** wording, cutoff, resolution source, collateral, and payout must match; near-matches are basis trades.
3. **Maker-first market making:** post-only quotes, inventory skew, stale cancels, small limits, fee/rebate lookup per market.
4. **Calibrated niche models:** versioned data, Brier score by bucket, timestamp checks, and abstention.
5. **Near-resolution sweeps:** defer; small apparent gains hide dispute, oracle, latency, and resolution tails.

No event trade passes without fair probability, calibration version, source timestamps, executable size, fees, expected slippage, worst-case partial-fill P&L, capital lockup, and resolution specification.

## Drastic and Creative Options

- **Remove LLM debate from the hot path.** Deterministic scanners qualify candidates; one model explains or reviews them.
- **Run an inversion tournament.** Compare original signal, inverse, and no-trade under identical out-of-sample costs; never auto-deploy an inverse without confirmation.
- **Pivot to picks-and-shovels.** Sell reproducible backtest audits, paper/live parity checks, executable-arbitrage alerts, or hosted strategy-readiness reports.
- **Monetize workflow or maker economics where permitted.** Builder/routing fees or maker rebates require platform, legal, tax, and compliance review.
- **Stop autonomous prop trading after 90 days if no sleeve clears the gate.** Move capital to benchmarks and retain Augr as research infrastructure.

## 90-Day Turnaround Plan

Profitability cannot be optimized until Augr can measure it. Freeze discovery, preserve evidence, fix the ledger and simulator, test three to five deterministic candidates with walk-forward and realistic costs, shadow live quotes, and promote only one tiny-capital sleeve at a time.

## Promotion Gates and Kill Criteria

Require at least 100 independent closed trades or 50 complete slower option cycles; positive after-cost out-of-sample alpha with uncertainty; acceptable drawdown, expected shortfall, skew, recovery, beta, and concentration; paper/live fill gap below 20% of gross edge; total operating cost below 10%–20% of expected gross edge; and exact reconciliation. Prediction arbitrage must remain positive in the worst permitted partial-fill state. Wheel total return must compete with PUT/BXM/BXMD—premium collected is never a KPI.

For 13F replication, replay at least 20 quarterly filing events across multiple managers using only information available after publication. Report achievable follower return, benchmark alpha, tracking error, turnover, mapping coverage, publication lag, drift, and cost sensitivity. Reject managers whose apparent edge depends on quarter-end look-ahead, confidential omissions, one concentrated winner, or fills at prices unavailable after filing.

Portfolio guardrails: daily loss limit, weekly drawdown pause, per-underlying and short-volatility caps, event calendar, stale-data breaker, and automatic no-trade when provenance is incomplete.

## Caveats, Sources, and Reproducibility

The audit uses an August 14, 2026 production database snapshot, repository code/documents, current exchange/regulatory material, scholarly research, and a read-only review of copy-trading commit `5517405` on `main`. The +$17.86 is a narrow cross-ledger reconciliation, not a time-weighted return or account statement. Ten open Kalshi positions lack marks; recorded fees and model cost are zero; taxes, financing, data, infrastructure, subscriptions, and engineering time are excluded.

The copy-trading assessment is code readiness, not performance analysis. The audited production database remains at schema 62 and contains no copy-trading tables, subscriptions, intents, fills, or returns. The complete Go test suite passed in a temporary checkout of `main`; the frontend was inspected but not rebuilt because workspace dependencies were not installed.

No strategy is guaranteed profitable. Options, prediction markets, and copied securities portfolios can lose the full risk budget. Broker permissions plus legal, tax, platform-terms, investment-adviser/broker-dealer, communications, recordkeeping, privacy, and jurisdictional review are required before any user-facing live copy feature. Sources and exact SQL are available through the report source panel.
